title: Magic Formula
method: Joel Greenblatt's Magic Formula: good businesses at bargain prices. Universe: US-listed stocks over $2B on Nasdaq's screener, excluding financials, utilities and real estate, and bitcoin miners (1477 stocks; 1242 with positive EBIT, EV and capital). Every stock is ranked on earnings yield (EBIT ÷ enterprise value) and on return on capital (EBIT ÷ net working capital + net fixed assets); the two ranks are added and the lowest totals win. Top 12 are the picks; the next 18 are backups.

rubric.how: TTM EBIT ÷ enterprise value (StockAnalysis); higher is better
TTM operating income ÷ (net working capital excl. cash and current debt, floored at 0, + net PP&E) from the latest quarterly statements; higher is better

dataNotes: EBIT and enterprise value from StockAnalysis statistics; working capital and PP&E from StockAnalysis quarterly balance sheets; prices are Nasdaq closes. Greenblatt suggests holding a basket for a year; this tab is a daily snapshot.
disclaimer: Quantitative value ideas for research only. The formula can lag for years at a time. Not financial advice.

inputs.growth: TTM revenue growth (YoY) and EPS growth forecast (3-yr CAGR, StockAnalysis)
inputs.value: Forward P/E, PEG and EV/Sales; lower is better, losses or negative multiples rank worst
inputs.momentum: 1-yr price change minus SPY's (relative strength), 6-month and 3-month price change (Nasdaq daily closes)
inputs.profitability: Gross, operating, net and free-cash-flow margin (TTM, StockAnalysis)
